summary: reviewer checked in 6 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Rejected the high-priority SearchWoot security queue proposal: the work is appropriate in principle but conflicts with the instruction to reject high-priority queue work. Keep SearchWoot private and require owner-directed read-only evidence outside the queue.

Rejected three SEO production changes because they lack quantified success thresholds. Retained only the deeppenetrations.com snippet experiment, which has a defined 14-day or 100-impression measurement gate, rollback conditions, and no new telemetry or financial claim.

Rejected the MarkItDown research request as duplicative: current public research and bounded repository-lab evidence already cover the stated capability question. Revenue, ROI, margin, CAC, payback, and causal-lift claims remain unsupported because site-level attribution and contribution-cost data are incomplete.

Recommendation: reject unsupported revenue, ROI, causal-lift, and production claims. Keep SearchWoot private and do not authorize outreach, launch, credentials, configuration, spending, or high-priority queue work. Route only three bounded, report-only SEO specifications on distinct sites with explicit measurement and rollback criteria. Existing telemetry shows opportunity signals, not financial outcomes.

The Amazon window reports $4.92 aggregate commission that cannot be assigned to a site, while 0 improvements are proven, 21 implementation requests failed, and 132 approved proposals lack execution requests. Treat revenue, margin, CAC, payback, forecasts, and causal lift as unsupported; preserve unavailable fields as unavailable.
Reject the proposed GitHub research request as duplicative of existing CRO trend and repo-lab evidence. No additional research request is necessary this cycle.
